narration: Giants of Karnataka: Dancing Under 40-Kilo Dolls
This is Gaarudi Gombe. Ancient origin legend; contemporary living folk dance.
on_screen: Title card: Gaarudi Gombe · India · Ancient origin legend; contemporary living folk dance

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Gaarudi Gombe is a folk dance originating in the state of Karnataka, India.
According to local legend, the performance traces back to the epic Mahabharata, where Lord Krishna soothed the anger of his wife Satyabhama by wearing a giant magical doll frame.
Historically and today, the tradition is integrated into major public festivities, including the famous Mysore Dasara procession.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Gaarudi Gombe is performed during major religious and cultural festivals, including the Mysore Dasara procession in Karnataka.
The main aesthetic intent is to create a funny, lighthearted atmosphere for the gathered crowds, while simultaneously serving a ritual purpose as a protective medium to ward off evil spirits.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dancer steps into the central opening beneath the massive frame from the underside, resting the wooden frame directly onto their shoulders.
Because the entire structure can reach 10 to 12 feet in height and weigh up to 40 kg, the dancer looks through a small opening in the frame to navigate.
Movement consists of balancing the heavy frame while shifting weight, turning, and stepping through street processions.
Watch for Frame Sway.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The defining element of the performance is the giant doll-suit (Gaarudi Gombe).
The face of the doll is constructed using a wooden basket coated with papier-mâché, painted with detailed sketches and pigments, and mounted on a sturdy wooden and bamboo frame.
The complete structure stands 10 to 12 feet tall and weighs up to 40 kg.

scenes.title: The people
narration: In the coastal districts of Karnataka, the tradition is known by the regional variant name Tattiraya, which highlights the carrying of bamboo stick structures.
The dance is a recognized Indian folk dance form from Karnataka.
